name: str_match_all
title: Extract every match and its capture groups

origin.description: Extract every match and its capturing groups. A string with no match contributes a matrix with no rows.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A regular expression. fixed, coll, boundary, and the empty string are errors. The pattern should contain at least one capturing group.

origin.details: Recycling and names follow str_match. Each matrix has the same columns as str_match and one row for each match. A miss is omitted. A missing string is one row of missing values. A group that did not participate is missing. Named groups name the columns of each matrix.
origin.value: A list of character matrices, one for each element of string or pattern.

translation.description: Extract every match and its capturing groups. A string with no match contributes a matrix with no rows.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, stringi._na.NA, or a list of those. A list may carry names.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A plain string, list, or regex() pattern. fixed, coll, boundary, and the empty string raise ValueError. The message is that pattern must be a regular expression.

translation.details: check_lengths raises RecycleError when lengths other than 0 and 1 disagree. pattern_type must be regex. The call is stri_match_all_regex with omit_no_match=True and pattern_opts. Each element is a character matrix. A miss has no rows. A missing string is one row of NA. Named groups are stored on colnames. Names on string are kept when pattern has length 1 or the same length as string.
translation.value: A list of character matrices. Each matrix is a list of rows, and a missing cell is stringi._na.NA, which is JSON null.
translation.example:
from stringi._na import NA
from stringr.match import str_match_all
x = ["<a> <b>", "<a> <>", "<a>", "", NA]
print(str_match_all(x, "<(.*?)>"))
